question:
In \(\triangle ABC,\) \(AB=8,\) \(BC=7,\) \(CA=6\) and side \(BC\) is extended, as shown in the figure, to a point \(P\) so that \(\triangle PAB\) is similar to \(\triangle PCA.\) The length of \(PC\) is

[Figure 1](figures/1986_AMC_12_Q16_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The order in \(\triangle PAB\sim\triangle PCA\) gives the correspondence \(P\leftrightarrow P\), \(A\leftrightarrow C\), and \(B\leftrightarrow A\). Thus \(AB\) corresponds to \(CA\), so the ratio of corresponding sides is
\[
\frac{AB}{CA}=\frac{8}{6}=\frac43.
\]
The segment \(PA\) appears in both triangles in different roles. Using both of its corresponding-side ratios lets us eliminate it:
\[
\frac{PA}{PC}=\frac43,
\qquad
\frac{PB}{PA}=\frac43.
\]
Multiplying gives
\[
\frac{PB}{PC}=\frac{16}{9}.
\]
Let \(x=PC>0\). The figure places \(C\) between \(P\) and \(B\), so \(PB=x+7\). Therefore
\[
\frac{x+7}{x}=\frac{16}{9}.
\]
Since \(x>0\), cross multiplication is valid. It gives
\[
9x+63=16x,
\qquad 63=7x,
\qquad x=9.
\]
This positive value gives \(PA=12\) and \(PB=16\); the three corresponding side ratios are \(12/9=16/12=8/6=4/3\), and \(PB-PC=7\). Thus \(PC=\boxed{9}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
